workflow: A native operation invokes a user callback through a registered context pointer without retaining ownership of that context.
The callback reentrantly removes or replaces its registration, causing cleanup to release the context while the outer invocation is still active.
Callback machinery resumes and accesses or cleans up the released context through the stale pointer.
The stale dereference causes a use-after-free failure and process termination instead of a recoverable callback error.
summary: Reentrant callback deregistration releases active callback context
decision_reason: The underlying failure is materially the same as retained-pointer use-after-free: an active operation keeps a pointer reachable while reentrant mutation releases the pointer's owning storage. The callback-registration and reentrancy details are implementation-specific variants of that workflow.
